claims.value: SILAC light = pre-existing proteins; SILAC heavy = proteins synthesised during the labelling period (same culture, same run)
claims.evidence: Paper Methods/PRIDE protocol: "quiescent fibroblasts were switched to media containing stable heavy isotopes of lysine and arginine (13C6-Lysine, 13C6, 15N4-Arginine) for 1 to 6 days"; Fig. 1 legend: % 12C ("old") remaining vs % 13C-labelled ("new"). Supp Data 1: "%heavy isotope ... after 0, 2, 4 and 6 days of labeling". Data check (heavy_frac): passing heavy-search PSMs rise with labelling time in every file (WT 0D ~1%, 1D 27%, 2D 36-37%, 4D 50-53%, 6D 58-61%; HGPS 0D 2-18%, 1D 29-32%, 2D 44-48%, 4D 76%, 6D 71-77%) and Supp Data 1 median %heavy WT 5.3/28.0/45.9/60.5, HGPS 2.1/41.2/64.6/77.8 at 0/2/4/6 D -> heavy = new. Both channels come from one culture, so they share biological replicate 1 and get distinct source names (precedent PXD028934). 0D rows: the paper calls 0D "no label" (Fig. 1c: "after no label (c, 473 proteins)"), so the 0D heavy rows are a background channel (heavy-search PSMs 0.7-1.8% in WT, 1.8-17.9% in HGPS), not newly synthesised protein. They are kept because each 0D run was searched for heavy peptides and Supp Data 1 has a 0D sheet.

claims.location: characteristics[sampling time], factor value[sampling time], characteristics[subcellular fraction], factor value[subcellular fraction], characteristics[cellular component] rows 1-26
claims.value: N day from file name (0D,1D,2D,4D,6D); nuclear extract / nuclear pellet; nucleus
claims.evidence: Run names <date>_WT_<N>D_<extract|pellet>[_2].ms2 and mzid names WT_<N>D_<extract|pellet>.mzid. PRIDE/paper: "Crude nuclei were extracted in 10 mM Tris pH 8, 1% n-octyl glucoside, 400 mM NaCl, and 1 mM DTT, and extracts and pellets were prepared separately for LC-MS/MS". Sampling time = days in heavy medium before harvest; confirmed by the monotonic heavy fraction (heavy_frac). cellular component nucleus = GO:0005634. Extract and pellet are distinct measured samples -> characteristics + factor (rule 16); characteristics[subcellular fraction] is a custom column (curated precedent name).
One labelling culture per time point; each (time, fraction) group contains one culture (rule 3). Files with suffix _2 are repeat injections -> comment[technical replicate] 2.

RawConverter .ms2 files were renamed after conversion: the mzid SpectraData point to 2016MMDD_MHAB-N_<MP|SCX|SCXtip>[ _2].mzXML. Each .ms2 LastScan equals exactly one same-date mzXML scanCount: WT_0D_extract=MHAB-1_SCXtip (122811), _2=MHAB-1_SCXtip_2 (126007), WT_0D_pellet=MHAB-2_SCXtip (119100; first MS2 precursor 414.71 identical), _2=MHAB-2_SCXtip_2 (119451), WT_1D_extract=MHAB-3_MP (95539), WT_1D_pellet=MHAB-4_MP (131043), WT_2D_extract=MHAB-5_SCX (119867), WT_2D_pellet=MHAB-6_SCX (123219), WT_6D_extract=MHAB-9_SCX (115889), WT_6D_pellet=MHAB-10_SCX (126287), WT_4D_extract=MHAB-7_SCX (104793), _2=MHAB-7_SCX_2 (120876), WT_4D_pellet=MHAB-8_SCX (121397). Every mzid name (WT_<N>D_<fraction>) points to the MHAB-N file mapped to the same-named .ms2, which confirms the mapping.

limitations: PRIDE project-level identifiedPTMStrings (MOD:00425 monohydroxylated residue, MOD:00394 acetylated residue, MOD:00397 iodoacetamide derivatized residue) conflict with the deposited searches: no oxidation or acetylation appears in any mzid SearchModification list, and the protocol alkylation was chloroacetamide (the 57.021 C mass is the same as carbamidomethyl). The SDRF follows the mzid (rule 5).

WT_1D_pellet.mzid is byte-identical to WT_1D_extract.mzid (both point to MHAB-3_MP = WT_1D_extract): the search of 20160302_WT_1D_pellet.ms2 (= MHAB-4_MP) is not deposited. Its modification parameters (no CAM/phospho, labels only) and tolerances are inferred from the other three 1D searches (WT_1D_extract, HGPS_1D_extract, HGPS_1D_pellet), all identical; not documented for this file.

PARTIAL SCOPE (recorded in annotations/BLOCKED.md, section PXD006015): two WT PEAK-only mzXML files, 20160302_MHAB-1_MP.mzXML (121771 scans) and 20160302_MHAB-2_MP.mzXML (103970 scans), are not annotated. By the MHAB numbering that maps every other run (WT MHAB-1..10 / HGPS MHAB-11..20 = 0D,1D,2D,4D,6D x extract,pellet) they are the WT 0 day nuclear extract and pellet, re-run after the "MP" clean-up on 20160302, the same day as HGPS 0D MHAB-11_MP/12_MP. They are excluded because they have no RAW-category .ms2, no deposited mzid references them (the WT_0D mzids use only the MHAB-1/2_SCXtip runs), so their search is undocumented, and their clean-up differs from the searched SCXtip runs. The identity rests on file numbering only.
The PRIDE files carry 13 .ms2 RAW files; the paper's Supp Data 1 has no 1D sheet, and the WT 1D searches yielded few PSMs (424 light + 161 heavy for WT_1D_extract).
The WT/HGPS comparison spans two deposits (PXD006015 WT, PXD006016 HGPS); each SDRF carries one disease state, so the cross-deposit comparison is not encoded as a factor here.

No vendor .raw files are deposited (none of PXD006012-PXD006016 has one); comment[data file] lists the RawConverter .ms2 files that PRIDE categorises as RAW. The .mzXML (PEAK) copies are not listed. Reprocessing from the SDRF will need .ms2/.mzXML-capable tools.

SILAC culture medium is not stated (paper: cells grown in MEM + 15% FBS for general culture; SILAC media base not named) -> characteristics[culture medium] not available. Passage stated only as "<20" -> not available. Storage temperature not stated.
Quiescence (1% serum for 3-5 days before harvest/labelling) applies to every sample and is encoded only in the source names, not as a treatment column.
